reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently against psalm_device_inventory.json: 145's genre_label_membership shows tehillah = [145] only (1 of 150 WEB titles), and its acrostics entry gives first_letters_mt matching the full alphabet with only nun absent -- both cited counts hold. Byte-collated the three Hebrew anchors and all three curly-quoted WEB verses against verse_map_oshb.json / verse_map_web.json; all matched verbatim. The identity-psalm framing (title inside MT v1, web:Ps.145.0 = oshb:Ps.145.1) matches Psalm 145's placement outside both the shift+1 and shift+2 rosters and the owner-ruled title-equation form. The rejected_alternative correctly isolates the register break at web:Ps.145.4 (first-person vow to third-person report of what generations will do); no rival seam inside 145:1-3 competes with the alef/bet/gimel run. Confidence=high is warranted: tier-1 acrostic-letter evidence plus a title-genre fact both check out byte-true, and the span boundary has textual support on both sides.

Byte-collated all four Hebrew acrostic anchors (dalet/he/waw/zayin) and all three curly-quoted WEB verses against the source maps; verbatim matches throughout. The ketiv/qere claim at web:Ps.145.6 checks against pmarks_Ps.json's kq inventory, which does carry an entry keyed 'Ps.145.6' (one of the 65 K/Q verses book-wide) -- the row's disclosure is accurate and correctly scoped to the single verse. The rejected_alternative's register break at web:Ps.145.8 (third-person generational report to direct predication of Yahweh's own character) is the same kind of tier-1 grammatical-subject shift used elsewhere in this psalm's segmentation and holds up against the actual verse content. No rival seam presents inside dalet-zayin. Confidence=high is justified.

Byte-collated all six Hebrew acrostic anchors (het through mem) and all six curly-quoted WEB verses; verbatim matches throughout, including the longest quote in the cluster at web:Ps.145.13. Independently checked the variant-zone claim at the byte level: oshb Ps.145.13 carries exactly two clauses (kingdom/dominion) with no nun-initial sentence, while the WEB text for the same ref carries a third, nun-initial sentence ('Yahweh is faithful...') absent from the MT bytes -- confirming the row's disclosure that the acrostic's one surface gap (21 of 22 letters, nun missing per psalm_device_inventory.json) is handled correctly: the row does not select a reading, and correctly notes the variant without treating the WEB-only sentence as MT acrostic content. The rejected_alternative (isolating web:Ps.145.13 as its own row) is a legitimate option the row considered and reasonably declined given MT's own bytes tie v13 to the kingdom-glory language of vv11-12 with no independent seam before it. Confidence=medium is appropriately calibrated to the added complexity of the variant-zone disclosure inside an otherwise ordinary strophe.

Verified first letters directly from oshb bytes: web:Ps.145.14 opens samekh (סומֵףאְוֹמֵף-pattern), .15 opens ayin, .16 opens pe -- matching the row's samekh/ayin/pe sequence exactly, and correctly picking up immediately after 145:13's mem, consistent with the acrostic's own letter-skip over nun. All three curly-quoted WEB verses byte-matched their sources. The rejected_alternative's boundary at web:Ps.145.17 (provision imagery giving way to a righteousness/nearness declarative catalog) holds: 145:17 does open a fresh catalog on tsade with a different predicate pattern. No rival seam competes inside samekh-pe. Confidence=high is justified.

Verified first letters directly from oshb bytes for all five verses: tsade(17), qof(18), resh(19), shin(20), tav(21) -- exact match to the row's claimed sequence and to the acrostic's own closing letter. Byte-collated the two Hebrew anchors and both curly-quoted WEB verses; verbatim. The root-recurrence claim (tehillat at 145:21 sharing its root with the title's tehillah at 145:0) is accurate -- both forms derive from the same halal root, a legitimate inclusio observation tying the psalm's close back to its opening genre label. The rejected_alternative's proposed split (righteousness/nearness couplet vs answered-cry/preserve-destroy verses) is reasonably declined: the catalog does run unbroken tsade-tav with no addressee or mode shift internal to it. Confidence=high is justified; this row correctly closes the psalm at its own final acrostic letter.

Verified the hallelu-Yah count independently against psalm_device_inventory.json's halleluyah object: verse_initial lists Ps.146.1 among 11 occurrences (counts.verse_initial = 11), matching the row's claim exactly. Byte-collated the Hebrew frame anchor and both curly-quoted WEB verses; verbatim matches. The rejected_alternative's register break at web:Ps.146.3 (cohortative first-person self-address 'my soul' to direct second-person imperative admonition) is a strong tier-1 speech-act shift and the row correctly declines to fold it in. Confidence=high is justified.

The span and warrant are sound: the negative imperative at web:Ps.146.3 is a genuine fresh speech-act with no earlier imperative counterpart in the psalm, and the mortality clause at web:Ps.146.4 stays within the same subject the imperative introduces -- a defensible strophe. The rejected_alternative (declining to extend through 146:5's beatitude, since its opening particle answers the admonition with a positively-framed unit) is sound. However the row fails byte-verbatim quote fidelity on its own curly-quoted WEB text, which is grounds for a challenge under this book's quote-fidelity requirement even though the underlying warrant is fine.

challenges.claim: The row's curly-quoted WEB text for web:Ps.146.3 substitutes a straight apostrophe for the source's typographic apostrophe, so the quote is not byte-verbatim.
challenges.evidence: Source verse_map_web.json text at web:Ps.146.3: “Don’t put your trust in princes, in a son of man in whom there is no help.” -- note the right single quotation mark U+2019 inside “Don’t”. The row's rationale instead renders this word with a plain ASCII apostrophe U+0027 (“Don't put your...”), a byte mismatch against the source even though the outer curly double quotes are correctly formed.

reviews.reasoning: The participle count is independently re-derived and confirmed exact: reading MT 146:6-9 directly from oshb bytes gives nine Qal/Hifil active participles (עֹשֶַׂה/הַש׉ֹמֵר in v6, עֹשֶַׂה/נֹתֵן/מַתִׁיר in v7, פֹּ׈קֵ׈ַח/זֹקֵף/אֹהֵב in v8, ש׉ֹטֵ׈ם in v9), matching the row's own word list, and byte-collation of every Hebrew anchor and every curly-quoted WEB verse in this row is verbatim. The row also correctly separates the two finite Piel imperfects at the close of v9 (יְעוֹדֱֵד, יְעַוֵּּת) from the participle chain, which is an accurate morphological distinction given the source bytes. That said, the row's own rejected_alternative already surfaces the live rival: whether web:Ps.146.10 belongs inside this strophe or stands alone as the psalm's closing frame-row (mirroring how 146:1-2 stands alone as the opening frame-row). The form-shift at the v9|v10 seam is at least as strong as the shifts this same cluster treats as boundary-driving elsewhere: v6-9 runs an unbroken chain of participles (habitual-aspect predication, third-person objects -- the blind, the bowed, foreigners, the fatherless/widow, the wicked), while v10 shifts to a finite imperfect proclamation (יִמְלֹךְ, 'he will reign') with a direct second-person vocative addressee change to Zion (אֱלֹהַַיִךְ צִּיּוֹן, 'your God, Zion'). That is the same class of tier-1 grammatical-subject/addressee shift the row itself uses to separate 146:1-2 from 146:3-4 and 146:3-4 from 146:5-. The row's counter-argument (the hallelu-Yah frame closes within v10, making it this strophe's own capstone) is a real literary point but it argues for the whole psalm's inclusio, not specifically for binding v10 to the participle catalog rather than treating it as the frame's own closing row -- the same frame logic would equally support the alternative row-policy shape (opening frame row / body / closing frame row). Confidence=medium already reflects the row's own awareness that this seam is unsettled; the segmentation should be treated as genuinely contestable rather than settled by the capstone framing alone.

challenges.claim: web:Ps.146.10 has a tier-1 grammatical/addressee shift from the v6-9 participle chain (third-person habitual predication) to a finite imperfect proclamation with direct address to Zion, giving a legitimate rival seam at 146:9|146:10 that the row's frame-closure rationale does not fully foreclose.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.146.9 closing verb: שֹׁ֘מֵ֤ר (participle, continuing the v6-8 chain); oshb:Ps.146.10 opening form: יִמְלֹ֤ךְ (Qal imperfect 3ms 'he will reign', not a participle) followed by the direct-address phrase אֱלֹהַ֣יִךְ צִ֭יּוֹן ('your God, Zion' -- 2fs suffix, vocative). “Yahweh will reign forever; your God, O Zion, to all generations.” (web:Ps.146.10). This is the same form-class of shift (predicate-pattern change plus addressee change) that the row's own siblings in this cluster treat as boundary-driving at 146:2|146:3 and 146:4|146:5.
